blocks.text: **Backtracking** finds every solution — or one that works — by building it **one choice at a time**. At each step it tries a choice, carries on with the rest, and when that line of choices is finished or turns out to be a dead end, it **undoes** the choice and tries the next. It's how you'd solve a maze by hand: walk forward, and at a dead end, go back to the last fork and take another path.

blocks.alt: The decision tree for all binary strings of length 2. From the start, choose 0 or 1; from each, choose 0 or 1 again. The four leaves, 00, 01, 10 and 11, are the answers. Backtracking walks this tree depth-first: start, 0, 00, back up, 01, back up twice, 1, 10, back up, 11.

blocks.text: Every backtracking function has the same three moves around a recursive call:

items: **Choose** — make one choice and record it in the current **path** (the partial solution).
**Explore** — call the function again to make the remaining choices.
**Un-choose** — remove the choice from the path, restoring things exactly as they were, so the next choice starts clean.

blocks.text: When the path is complete — here, when it holds n bits — it's an answer: copy it into the results and return. The function never needs to know how deep it is in the tree; the path and the recursion remember that.

blocks.caption: The tree grows as the search goes deeper; each time a choice is undone, the search backs up to the last fork.

blocks.code:
def binary_strings(n):
    result, path = [], []                 # path: the choices made so far

    def build():
        if len(path) == n:                # a full string: record it
            result.append("".join(path))
            return
        for bit in "01":
            path.append(bit)              # choose
            build()                       # explore
            path.pop()                    # un-choose

    build()
    return result

blocks.text: How it walks the tree, and what it costs

Backtracking is a **depth-first traversal of the decision tree** — the call stack holds the current path from the top down to where the search is. Nothing else is stored: the tree is never built in memory, only walked.

items: **Time** — proportional to the number of tree nodes visited: here 2ⁿ leaves (and about as many inner nodes), and copying each n-letter answer: **O(2ⁿ · n)**.
**Space** — the path and the call stack are at most **n** deep: **O(n)** extra, besides the output itself.
That's the trade: backtracking is exponential in time, because it really tries everything, but very light on memory.
**Generate everything**: all subsets, combinations, permutations, valid bracket strings, phone-keypad words.
**Find a solution under constraints**: N-Queens, Sudoku, crosswords, word search in a grid.
**Optimisation by search**: try every arrangement but **prune** the ones that can't beat the best so far (next lesson).
Backtracking = **choose, explore, un-choose**, repeated at every level.
It's a **depth-first walk** of the decision tree; leaves are complete answers.
Time grows with the number of tree nodes (often exponential); space is only the **depth**.
Always undo exactly what you did, and copy the path when you record an answer.
